TASK -- client-side chat UI refactor (plan Step 6).

Route contract you are consuming (from the agent who built the routes): POST /api/chat
Request JSON: { id: string; messages: Array<{ id: string; role: "system"|"user"|"assistant"; parts: Array<{type:string; ...}> }>; eventId: unknown (coerced server-side via z.coerce.string()); threadId: string | null }. Body is validated with a zod schema built from z.looseObject so extra UIMessage fields (metadata, extra part fields) pass through untouched.
Response on validation failure: plain (non-streaming) `Response`, status 400, JSON `{ "error": "Invalid request body" }`.
Response on success: `createUIMessageStreamResponse({ stream })` -- an SSE `text/event-stream` body carrying AI SDK UIMessageChunk JSON objects (the standard AI SDK v6 UI Message Stream protocol, not the backend's raw event names). Exact chunk objects written by the adapter, in order:
1. `{ type: "start", messageId: <generateId() from "ai"> }`
2. `{ type: "data-thread", id: "thread", data: { threadId: string }, transient: true }` -- written once, immediately after start; transient:true means the AI SDK does not fold it into the persisted message history, and store.upsertMessage additionally strips any part with type "data-thread" as defense in depth. This is how the client learns the resolved/newly-created thread id (via its onData handler for the "data-thread" wire type).
3. `{ type: "data-sources", id: "sources", data: ChatSource[] }` -- written exactly once (even if the array is empty) when the backend's `sources` SSE event arrives. `data` is the full ChatSource[] array (fields: document_id, chunk_id, title, url, source_name, published_at, tickers, classification, similarity, excerpt) -- this part is what the client persists/renders as the source list.
4. Zero or more `{ type: "source-url", sourceId: <source.document_id>, url: <source.url> }` -- one per source that has a non-null url, written immediately after data-sources, for native AI-SDK source rendering interop.
5. `{ type: "text-start", id: "text" }` -- written the first time a backend `delta` event arrives (not written at all if zero deltas occur).
6. Zero or more `{ type: "text-delta", id: "text", delta: <token text> }` -- one per backend `delta` event.
7. `{ type: "text-end", id: "text" }` -- written when the backend's terminal `done` or `error` event arrives, but only if text-start was previously written (paired defensively).
8. Terminal: on backend `done`, execute() returns normally and the AI SDK appends its own `finish` chunk. On backend `error` OR any fetch/network failure (including non-2xx from POST /api/chat/stream, e.g. the backend's pre-stream 400/502), the adapter throws inside execute(); the AI SDK then invokes onError, which returns the fixed string "The research backend is unavailable. Please try again." -- surfaced to the client as a UI message stream error chunk. No backend error detail (e.g. the backend's own {"message": ...}) is ever forwarded, and there is no code path returning HTTP 200 with placeholder assistant text.
Side effects: BEFORE calling the backend, the last message in the incoming `messages` array is upserted verbatim (id/role/parts) via store.upsertMessage(threadId, ...) so a mid-stream failure still leaves the question saved. In onFinish, if the assistant responseMessage's concatenated text parts are non-empty, it is upserted the same way (partial text from an abort/crash is intentionally kept); touchThread(threadId) is always called in onFinish regardless of whether text was empty.
Thread resolution: if body.threadId is present, getThreadIfOwned(threadId, sessionId) is tried first; on a null result (missing/forged/foreign id) or no threadId given, a new thread is lazily created via createThread(sessionId, eventId, title) where title = the full text of the first role:"user" message in `messages` (store.createThread truncates to 80 chars itself).
Env var: BACKEND_URL (server-only) is read first, falling back to the existing NEXT_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL, then "http://localhost:8000". The adapter POSTs to `${BACKEND_URL}/api/chat/stream` with body `{ messages: [{ role, content }, ...] }` where content = concatenation (joined with "") of every part with type "text" in that message's parts array, for every message in the incoming array in original order (no client-side capping -- the backend caps history itself).
Cookie (both routes): name "sl_anon_session", set via `(await cookies()).set(name, value, { httpOnly: true, sameSite: "lax", path: "/", maxAge: 31536000 })` (31536000 = 60*60*24*365 seconds) only when not already present on the incoming request.

GET /api/chat/thread?eventId=<string>
Missing eventId: `Response`, status 400, JSON `{ "error": "Missing eventId query param" }`.
Otherwise 200 JSON: `{ threadId: string; messages: ChatMessageRecord[] }` when a thread exists for (sessionId, eventId) via store.findThread + store.loadMessages, or `{ threadId: null, messages: [] }` when none exists yet. `ChatMessageRecord` (from src/lib/chat/store.ts) = `{ id: string; role: string; parts: unknown[] }`, ordered by seq ascending. Also mints the sl_anon_session cookie (same options as above) if the request doesn't already carry one -- this route is meant to run on chat panel mount, before the first POST.

Data part wire-type strings a client component must know: "data-thread" (transient, `{ threadId: string }`), "data-sources" (persisted, `ChatSource[]`), plus the native AI SDK "source-url" part (`{ sourceId, url }`). ChatSource and ChatUIMessage types are unchanged, imported from src/types/chat.ts (not modified by this task).

No new npm dependencies were added; `ai` (^6.0.246) and `zod` (^4.4.3) were already in package.json. Zod v4 API used: z.looseObject (not the deprecated z.object().passthrough()) and z.coerce.string().
Chat types/modules available: All four files are new, under existing `src/` — no other files were modified (verified via `git status`: only these four appear as new untracked paths beyond pre-existing in-flight work).

1. src/lib/supabase/server.ts
   - export function getSupabaseServerClient(): SupabaseClient<Database>
   - Lazy singleton via module-level `let client: SupabaseClient<Database> | null = null`. Reads process.env.SUPABASE_URL and process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY (no NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix — server-only). Throws if either is missing, only at call time (not at import time). Options: { auth: { persistSession: false, autoRefreshToken: false } }.

2. src/lib/chat/sse.ts
   - export interface ParsedSSEEvent { event: string; data: unknown }
   - export async function* parseSSEStream(stream: ReadableStream<Uint8Array>): AsyncGenerator<ParsedSSEEvent>
   - Buffers chunks (TextDecoder with {stream:true}), splits on "\n\n", ignores lines starting with ":", parses "event:" and "data:" lines, JSON.parse's the data payload, yields {event, data}.

3. src/types/chat.ts
   - export interface ChatSource { document_id: string; chunk_id: string | null; title: string | null; url: string | null; source_name: string | null; published_at: string | null; tickers: string[]; classification: string | null; similarity: number; excerpt: string }
   - export type ChatDataParts = { sources: ChatSource[]; thread: { threadId: string } }  — MUST stay a `type`, not `interface` (interface fails the UIDataTypes/Record<string,unknown> generic constraint in strict mode).
   - export type ChatUIMessage = UIMessage<unknown, ChatDataParts>  (imports UIMessage from "ai"; installed ai version is 6.0.246, UIMessage generic order is <METADATA, DATA_PARTS, TOOLS>, all defaulted, so passing 2 args is valid). Data part type strings are "data-<key>", so the thread data part's wire type is "data-thread" — matches what store.ts filters out.

4. src/lib/chat/store.ts (imports getSupabaseServerClient from "@/lib/supabase/server"; imports Database, Json from "@/types/database.types")
   - export type ChatThreadRow = Database["public"]["Tables"]["chat_threads"]["Row"]
   - export interface ChatMessageRecord { id: string; role: string; parts: unknown[] }
   - export async function findThread(sessionId: string, eventId: string): Promise<ChatThreadRow | null>
   - export async function createThread(sessionId: string, eventId: string, title: string): Promise<ChatThreadRow>  — truncates title to 80 chars
   - export async function getThreadIfOwned(threadId: string, sessionId: string): Promise<ChatThreadRow | null>  — returns null if row doesn't exist or anon_session_id mismatch
   - export async function loadMessages(threadId: string): Promise<ChatMessageRecord[]>  — ordered by seq ascending
   - export async function upsertMessage(threadId: string, msg: { id: string; role: string; parts: unknown[] }): Promise<void>  — upserts on conflict "id"; strips any part with type === "data-thread" before persisting
   - export async function touchThread(threadId: string): Promise<void>  — issues `.update({ id: threadId }).eq("id", threadId)`, a no-op column update that still fires the update_chat_threads_timestamp BEFORE UPDATE trigger (which unconditionally sets NEW.updated_at = NOW())

Verification: `npx tsc --noEmit` from repo root exits 0 (confirmed twice, once with explicit `echo EXIT:$?`) — no errors in these four files and no pre-existing errors elsewhere. Nothing was staged, committed, or pushed; git status confirms only these four new files were added under src/lib/chat/, src/lib/supabase/, and src/types/chat.ts — all other diffs in the tree are pre-existing/unrelated in-flight work.

Read the current src/components/chat/ChatPanel.tsx first (it is a small hand-rolled useState chat loop, ~130 lines, that POSTs to /api/chat and ignores sources entirely -- no citation UI exists today). Also read src/components/leads/LeadDetailPanel.tsx to see how it is invoked: <ChatPanel event={detail?.event ?? null} /> where event is StockEvent | null and event.id is a string. Also skim the existing ui/ primitives you will reuse: src/components/ui/card.tsx, scroll-area.tsx, skeleton.tsx, badge.tsx, button.tsx, input.tsx -- match their existing visual conventions (this app currently uses small 11px text, muted-foreground colors, rounded-lg bubbles for chat -- keep that look).

Before writing useChat-based code, inspect node_modules/@ai-sdk/react's real type definitions/docs for the useChat hook's v6 API (message/parts shape, status values, stop(), regenerate(), sendMessage(), and whether input/handleSubmit are still managed by the hook or must be handled manually with local useState in this version) and node_modules/ai for DefaultChatTransport's options (api, prepareSendMessagesRequest) -- ground this against what is actually installed, not memory.

Write:

1. src/components/chat/ChatPanel.tsx (rewrite, ~110 lines): keep the outer Card/empty-state shell (renders a friendly empty state when event is null, matching the current look). When event is non-null, fetch GET /api/chat/thread?eventId=<event.id> in an effect keyed on event.id (show a Skeleton while loading), then render a new <ChatThread key={event.id} event={event} initialMessages={...} initialThreadId={...} /> -- the key={event.id} is load-bearing: it forces a full remount when the selected event changes, which is what fixes the existing stale-transcript bug where messages carried over between different events.

2. src/components/chat/ChatThread.tsx (new, ~150 lines): use the useChat hook (generic over the ChatUIMessage type) with { id: event.id, messages: initialMessages, transport: new DefaultChatTransport({ api: "/api/chat", prepareSendMessagesRequest: <inject { eventId: event.id, threadId: currentThreadIdRef.current } into the request body> }), onData: <update a threadIdRef when a "data-thread" part arrives> }. Manage the text input with local useState and call sendMessage({ text }) yourself on submit (do not rely on the hook's own managed input/handleSubmit if this installed version does not provide/recommend it for v6 -- check what you found in node_modules). Render message.parts in order: a "text" part renders with the existing bubble styling (user right-aligned, assistant left-aligned, matching the current visual style you read above); a "data-sources" part renders a <SourceList sources={...} />; a native "source-url" part is not separately rendered (skip it, data-sources is the UI's source of truth, source-url exists only for SDK interop). When status is "submitted" show a small "Searching filings…" shimmer/loading row. When there is an error, show an inline destructive-styled row with a Retry button that calls regenerate(). Auto-scroll to the bottom as new parts stream in (a bottom sentinel div plus a scroll effect keyed on the messages array). Show a Stop button (calls the hook's stop()) in place of the send button while status is "streaming".

3. src/components/chat/SourceList.tsx (new, ~70 lines): props = { sources: ChatSource[] }. A "Sources (N)" toggle that expands/collapses. Each source row: a "[n]" index matching the "[Source n]" numbering the backend LLM cites (1-based, in array order); the title as a link to url (fallback text "Untitled document" if title/url are null); source_name and a formatted published_at date; ticker Badge components (reuse the existing src/components/ui/badge.tsx) for each ticker; a similarity percentage; a muted excerpt line.

4. In src/types/leads.ts, remove the now-dead ChatMessage interface (the one with fields id/role/content/createdAt, currently around lines 54-59). First grep the whole src/ tree for other imports of that type to confirm ChatPanel.tsx was its only consumer -- if anything else still imports it, do not remove it and explain why in your notes instead. Only remove that one interface -- the rest of that file has unrelated pre-existing local edits you must not touch.

Run "npx tsc --noEmit" and "npm run lint" from the repo root afterward and fix any errors in the files you touched.

Return the component prop shapes and file list in keyDetails.
